paragraphs: Friend, most of this passage is about what your hand does when someone else is in need, and it ends by setting apart the firstborn animals for the LORD (Deuteronomy 15:7-8, 19). Moses tells Israel to open their hand, not shut it, and he says it again and again (Deuteronomy 15:7-8). Even the wicked thought he calls out, the one that looks at the calendar instead of the person, shows that God cares about the heart behind the gift (Deuteronomy 15:9). He says to give generously and not let your heart be grieved, and then the LORD will bless you in all your work (Deuteronomy 15:10).

So why would anybody live this way? Because of what Moses says to remember: "you were slaves in the land of Egypt, and the LORD your God redeemed you" (Deuteronomy 15:15). Everything Israel had, they got because God set them free first. That's why a freed servant leaves with plenty, not empty-handed, and why Moses says to give as the LORD has blessed you (Deuteronomy 15:13-14). Generosity comes from remembering what was given to you.

Here's what I want you to take back to your own kitchen, baker. Moses says there will never cease to be poor in the land, so the command to "open wide your hand" never goes out of date (Deuteronomy 15:11). Don't hand things over with a stingy face, and don't wait for a perfect moment to be kind. God has been generous with you, so the best thing you can do is pass it along with a glad heart. And Moses is NOT done preaching, so keep that apron on.
